issues.description: The Person model's attribute names are inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and template define Person with a 'firstName' property (getFirstName/setFirstName), but the solution's common model defines the field as 'givenName' with getGivenName/setGivenName. Meanwhile, the solution's server/service and the UI code still reference getFirstName/setFirstName and PropertyValueFactory("firstName"). This naming mismatch breaks the intended API/POJO contract and will cause compilation/runtime errors and confusion for students attempting to follow the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person model consistent across all artifacts. Restore the field name and accessor methods to 'firstName' (getFirstName/setFirstName) in the solution's src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java so they match the template and problem statement, or alternatively change all usages (service, controller, UI, and problem text) to consistently use 'givenName'. The simplest fix is to rename givenName/getGivenName/setGivenName in the solution to firstName/getFirstName/setFirstName.

issues.description: The Person first-name attribute is named inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement and the template model use 'firstName', but the solution's common Person model uses 'givenName'. Other solution code (PersonService, PersonScene, controllers) still reference 'firstName'. This mismatch (firstName vs givenName) breaks the conceptual mapping students rely on and will cause confusion and compilation/runtime errors in the solution codebase.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the first-name identifier consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename 'givenName' to 'firstName' in src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java in the solution repository and provide matching getter/setter names (getFirstName/setFirstName). Alternatively, update all usages (PersonService, PersonController, PersonScene, etc.) to use getGivenName/setGivenName consistently. Ensure the final names match the problem statement and the template to avoid extra cognitive load.
